fact_text: A UIN, or unique identification number, is assigned to each market participant, usually matching an individual investor's national ID number, so the exchange can track each player's trading.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: The UIN settlement report lists about 50 stocks with the highest volume and percentage gains, giving for each the settlement volume, settlement value and settlement percentage.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: The settlement ratio is the share of a stock's day volume that buyers took home as delivery, rather than shares that were bought and sold again within the same day.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: A high settlement ratio on meaningful volume suggests investors are accumulating and few traders are active, while ratios below 50%, such as 10% to 30%, point to heavy trader and intraday activity.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: A settlement ratio only means something with real volume; a stock trading a few hundred shares will show a near 100% ratio without signalling any real investor demand.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: WTL had an 86% settlement ratio in the UIN settlement report, meaning 86% of its traded volume was taken as delivery by buyers rather than squared within the same day.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: The analyst read WTL's 86% delivery ratio on healthy volume as possible knowledge of a coming positive development, which news would confirm or refute over about a month.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: Dividing a stock's UIN settlement value by its settled volume gives the average price at which investors who took delivery bought the shares.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: The analyst said that when a stock closes above the average delivery price, the buyers holding at that average may feel more confident, a check he said few investors use.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: Suraj Cotton Mills showed a settlement ratio of about 10,000% on a very small traded volume, which the analyst said carries little meaning for investor demand.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: The analyst said high-ratio, high-volume accumulation can reflect information not yet public, so he suggests watching such stocks alongside the news rather than trading against them.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)

fact_text: In the settlement example, Supernet Technology traded a volume of only 130 shares, which the analyst calls too thin to matter.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'UIN Settlement Report Explained | Who Is Buying & Selling in PSX?' (YouTube, 2025-05-10)
